facts.value: Kept the Jewish Law, regarded Jesus as a human Messiah rather than divine, used only a Gospel of Matthew and rejected Paul.

citations.excerpt: they held Cerinthian views on the person of Christ, used only the Gospel of Matthew (probably the Gospel according to the Hebrews—so Eusebius), and rejected Paul as an apostate from the Mosaic Law, to the customs and ordinances of which, including circumcision, they steadily adhered.
They denied the Divinity and the virginal birth of Christ; they clung to the observance of the Jewish Law ; they regarded St. Paul as an apostate

facts.value: A Jewish Christian movement whose name comes from an Aramaic word meaning poor men, found in Palestine, Cyprus, Asia Minor and Rome.

citations.excerpt: is a transliteration of an Aramean word meaning "poor men".
We find the sect of the Ebionites in Palestine and the surrounding regions, on the island of Cyprus, in Asia Minor, and even in Rome.
